facts.text: On this day in 1922, Howard Carter unsealed the inner chamber of Tutankhamun's tomb — but the discovery had already leaked. A canary eaten by a cobra on-site became Cairo's first viral omen.
On this day in 1832, the first streetcar in the world began service in New York City, pulled by horses along Fourth Avenue — a full 51 years before electric trams existed.
Monaco has a higher density of millionaires than any nation on Earth: roughly one in three residents qualifies, yet the country has no income tax and fits inside Central Park.
The world's largest city by area is not Tokyo or New York — it's Chongqing, China, whose municipal boundaries cover a territory larger than Austria, housing over 32 million people.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, containing roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface water — most of it in a boreal zone virtually no one lives near.

On this day in 1954, the Dow Jones Industrial Average finally reclaimed its 1929 pre-crash peak — 25 years after Black Tuesday. Investors who held through the Depression were technically whole again, in nominal terms.
On this day in 2013, Bitcoin crossed $1,000 for the first time. It had been worth less than a penny three years earlier.

The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 by 24 brokers who agreed to trade only with each other and charge fixed commissions. The cartel ran, largely unchallenged, for 180 years.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion — the largest in history — yet it listed on the Riyadh exchange only, after Wall Street banks balked at the liability of certifying its reserve estimates.
The entire U.S. bond market is roughly twice the size of the U.S. stock market, yet most retail investors couldn't name a single bond they own.

On this date in 1965, France became the third nation to launch a satellite — not with rockets borrowed from superpowers, but with a homegrown Diamant booster, quietly ending the American-Soviet duopoly on space.
On this date in 1922, Howard Carter unsealed Tutankhamun's burial chamber — but the real marvel is that the tomb's 3,300-year-old linen still contained intact DNA, readable by modern sequencers.
Your skeleton is not static. Every 10 years, almost all your bone mass has been silently demolished and rebuilt, cell by cell, so the skeleton you were born with no longer exists.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its interior would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Mantis shrimp see with 16 types of color receptors — four times more than humans — yet process color worse than we do. Evolution gave them hardware no software could use.
On this day in 1922, Howard Carter first peered into Tutankhamun's tomb. The pharaoh had been dead longer by then than the Roman Empire had existed.
On this day in 1944, a German V-2 rocket killed 168 people in a Woolworths in Deptford, London — the deadliest single rocket strike of the war, largely forgotten.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded.
The fax machine was invented before the telephone. Alexander Bain patented a working fax in 1843; Bell's telephone came in 1876.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.

Today in 1922, Howard Carter first peered into Tutankhamun's tomb. The ancient Egyptian word for it: 'per-djet' — house of eternity. English borrowed 'eternity' from Latin 'aeternitas', itself rooted in 'aevum': a lifetime, an age.
The Japanese word '木漏れ日' (komorebi) names the interplay of light and leaves when sunlight filters through a forest canopy. English has no single word for this. Japanese does, because it needed one.
Today in 1832, writer Mary Russell Mitford coined 'village green' in print, cementing a phrase so ordinary it now feels ancient. Words that feel timeless often have a precise, traceable birthday.

'Vellichor' is not an ancient word — it was coined in 2013 by John Koenig for his Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows. It means the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Invented words can feel immediately true.
The Old Norse 'ginnungagap' means the primordial void before creation — literally 'the yawning gap of gaps'. It is one of the oldest words in any Germanic language for absolute nothingness.

On this date in 2017, Bitcoin's price crossed $9,000 for the first time — but more quietly, SegWit adoption on the network had just surpassed 10%, a protocol shift that took years of political warfare to achieve.

On Nov 26, 2020, Ethereum's Beacon Chain deposit contract hit its 524,288 ETH threshold, locking in the proof-of-stake launch. Every depositor was blind to when — or whether — withdrawals would ever be enabled.
Bitcoin's smallest unit, the satoshi, wasn't named by Satoshi Nakamoto. The community chose the name in a 2010 Bitcointalk thread, long after the pseudonymous creator had already begun going silent.

The DAO hack in 2016 didn't exploit a flaw in Ethereum — it exploited a flaw in Solidity's reentrancy behavior that the language's own designers hadn't flagged as dangerous. The chain fork that followed was the real experiment.

Blockchain 'immutability' has a legal asterisk: the EU's GDPR right to erasure has never been reconciled with public ledgers. No regulator has yet forced a chain rewrite, but no court has ruled it categorically impossible.
On this date in 2022, ChatGPT launched publicly. It took 5 days to reach 1 million users — a milestone that took Netflix 3.5 years.
On this date in 2007, the ImageNet project began planning. The dataset it produced triggered the deep learning revolution by giving models 14 million labeled images to train on.
GPT-4 was trained on roughly 25,000 A100 GPUs running for 90 to 100 days — a compute bill estimated at over $100 million for a single training run.
AlphaFold 2 predicted the structure of nearly every known protein — about 200 million — in roughly 18 months. Experimental biology would have taken millennia to match that.
The transformer architecture, now the backbone of virtually every frontier AI model, was introduced in a 2017 paper written by eight authors, all of whom have since left Google.
